g.text: │ ││Covered moves and Copy types. Thought once that │
│ ││passing &v moves v. Next: borrowing rules, then │
│Two concepts are due. First, inner joins: how many rows does A INNER ││ │
│JOIN B return when one row matches? ││Inner join
│One row: an inner join keeps only the pairs that match. ││Self joins
│Correct. Now left joins, same tables: how many rows? ││
│Every row of A, so 3, with NULL in B's columns where nothing matched. ││
│We left off before borrowing. Predict what this prints: let v = vec![1, ││ │
│It compiles and prints 6 3. sum only borrows v. ││Mutable borrows
│Are you sure? Why doesn't passing it move v? ││ │
│&v only lends a reference, and the borrow ends when sum returns. ││
